_sources: DFRS (2015). State of Nepal's Forests. Department of Forest Research and Survey, Kathmandu. ISBN 978-9937-8896-3-6.
Hansen, M.C. et al. (2013). High-Resolution Global Maps of 21st-Century Forest Cover Change. Science 342(6160):850-853.
Global Forest Watch (2024). Nepal tree cover loss 2001-2024: national cumulative total ~58,320 ha. https://www.globalforestwatch.org/
Acharya, R.P. et al. (2018). Socio-economic factors and management regimes as drivers of tree cover change in Nepal. PeerJ 6:e4855.
World Bank (2025). Mapping Nepal's Forest Landscapes and Livelihoods. Washington DC.
FAO (2020). Global Forest Resources Assessment 2020 — Nepal Country Report.
_methodology: Risk Index (0-100) is a composite score normalized so the highest-risk district = 100. It is derived from three components weighted equally: (1) DFRS 2015 annual deforestation rate for the district's physiographic zone (Terai districts average ~1.3%/yr vs Hills ~0.3%/yr); (2) proportion of district land area under high agricultural/settlement encroachment pressure documented in World Bank 2025 and FAO 2020; (3) Churia (Siwalik) range degradation severity per DFRS 2015. District-level GFW tree cover loss hectares are NOT included because no authoritative district-disaggregated dataset is publicly available — Nepal's national total is ~58,320 ha (2001-2024) but no peer-reviewed source provides a verified per-district breakdown. Rankings reflect well-established scientific consensus that Terai/Madhesh districts face the highest deforestation pressure in Nepal.
_dataIntegrity: This index is transparent about what it cannot claim: exact per-district hectare figures are not available. The ranking order is supported by DFRS 2015, World Bank 2025, and peer-reviewed literature. Scores should be read as relative risk rankings, not absolute measurements.
